blocks.text: The MCP server currently exposes `zia_list_cloud_app_control_actions`, which returns the *available action types* for a given rule type and cloud application — but there is no tool to read the *configured* Cloud App Control rules (policies). This makes it impossible for an AI agent to audit or reason about which granular upload/download/chat restrictions are actually active in a tenant.

`zia_list_cloud_app_control_actions` returns a list of possible actions such as `DENY_AI_ML_UPLOAD`, `ALLOW_AI_ML_CHAT`, etc. for a given `rule_type` (e.g. `AI_ML`) and `cloud_apps` list. This is essentially the "menu" of what *could* be configured, not what *is* configured.
All other major ZIA policy areas follow a consistent pattern:

| Policy area | List tool | Get tool | |---|---|---| | URL Filtering | `zia_list_url_filtering_rules` | `zia_get_url_filtering_rule` | | SSL Inspection | `zia_list_ssl_inspection_rules` | `zia_get_ssl_inspection_rule` | | Web DLP | `zia_list_web_dlp_rules` | `zia_get_web_dlp_rule` | | Cloud Firewall | `zia_list_cloud_firewall_rules` | `zia_get_cloud_firewall_rule` | | **Cloud App Control** |  missing |  missing |
Two new tools following the existing naming convention:

blocks.item: `zia_list_cloud_app_control_rules(rule_type, search?)` — lists all configured Cloud App Control rules for a given policy type (e.g. `AI_ML`, `WEBMAIL`, `FILE_SHARE`)
`zia_get_cloud_app_control_rule(rule_type, rule_id)` — retrieves a single rule by ID

blocks.text: The underlying ZIA API endpoint already exists: `GET /zia/api/v1/cloudAppControlRules/{policy}` and `GET /zia/api/v1/cloudAppControlRules/{policy}/{id}`.

During a troubleshooting session using an AI agent (Claude via claude.ai with the Zscaler MCP), we investigated why a user could not upload files to ChatGPT. We were able to inspect URL filtering, SSL inspection, DLP rules, and cloud firewall — but had no way to verify whether a `DENY_AI_ML_UPLOAD` Cloud App Control rule was active. The agent had to fall back to a manual portal check, breaking the otherwise fully automated diagnostic workflow.
With `zia_list_cloud_app_control_rules`, the agent could have completed the full policy audit without leaving the MCP context.

blocks.item: Tested against: MCP server as integrated in claude.ai (version unclear, assumed ≤ v0.6.2)
Related tool already present: `zia_list_cloud_app_control_actions` (added in v0.6.2, PR #29)

blocks.text: @(user) Both tools you're requesting — `zia_list_cloud_app_control_rules` and `zia_get_cloud_app_control_rule` — already exist; they shipped in v0.11.0 ([PR #59](https://github.com/zscaler/zscaler-mcp-server/pull/59)), along with the full CAC rule CRUD family.

Your report notes you tested against an assumed ≤ v0.6.2 build, which predates that release — that's why the read tools weren't visible. They're category-scoped (rule_type required, e.g. AI_ML), with optional search and JMESPath query, and are part of the zia_cloud_app_control toolset.

Upgrading to the latest release (currently v0.12.4) should give you the exact DENY_AI_ML_UPLOAD audit capability your ChatGPT-upload investigation needed. Closing as already-implemented — let us know if a current build still shows the tools missing.
